memo.verdict: Neutral; park; conviction medium on the direction and low on the timing. Vimian is a 'Major Corporate Change' case that the share price has already paid for: good change, real early output, fully priced. At SEK 35.7 the modal return is about 5% a year over eighteen months and 8% a year over three years against the framework's 20% bar, so the 'Modal return' is F and the 'Investment Thesis' C; the same case at about SEK 29 clears the bar. The framework's park rule does not park the case (no D or F on management, business quality, predictability or trackability, all C); the return does. Two re-entry triggers: the price at or below about SEK 29 to 30 with the thesis intact (the eighteen-month test clears at SEK 29.4), or the Q3 2026 print on 22 October 2026 showing cash conversion above 60% and North American orthopaedics at mid-single-digit growth, which would move the re-rating branch's odds from 20% toward 35% and the 'Investment Case' from D to C while leaving the price question open. Invalidation: Q3 2026 cash conversion below 60% with net working capital still above 24% of revenue at year-end 2026, or Specialty Pharma underlying organic growth below 6% for two quarters.
case: The change is internal, broad and real. The board removed the chief executive on 17 July 2025 after eighteen months; the chief financial officer served as interim; Alireza Tajbakhsh, who built VetFamily from a regional purchasing group to over 10,000 member clinics with double-digit growth and margin expansion, became permanent from 24 November 2025 and took interim charge of MedTech himself from July 2025 to April 2026. A new leadership layer followed: Head of MedTech April 2026, Head of Specialty Pharma 1 October 2026, Head of M&A 5 October 2026 (replacing Martin Bengtson, 46 transactions); the board cut to five with three independent. Standards were raised in the weakest unit: US orthopaedics moved from inside sales to a field sales force in January 2026; more than 4,000 of 22,000 MedTech SKUs discontinued in Q4 2025; the annual order programme ended; Diagnostics production consolidated from four sites to two; over 80 senior managers through leadership programmes; KPIs standardised. A dental platform (iM3, AllAccem, Dental Focus, David AI) was built by acquisition and offset the US orthopaedic decline. Product entry is real and dated: 75 new products in twelve months; PAX2 (25 more allergens, launch H2 2026); Clarity XR (October 2025). Price rises of about 5% were implemented and wage inflation passed through, though against 10% to 12% veterinary cost inflation the real element is not demonstrated. Six of the framework's twelve internal forces are at B (chief executive, other leaders, standards improvement, new products, price rises, acquisitions), none at A; strategy is sharpened not changed (C); there is no guidance increase (D); no shareholder returns (F). The false-positive check is largely clean: no caretaker, no debt-funded buyback, no crown jewels sold, leverage stable at 2.1x; the 'PowerPoint transformation' flag is partly live in a EUR 300m 2030 target the sell-side does not model. Governance caps standards at B: no internal audit, self-assessments only, 12 whistleblower complaints in 2025. The incentive plan (LTIP 2026/2029, 70% on FY2028 adjusted EBITA, 30% on revenue, hurdles undisclosed, no return-on-capital metric, no clawback) aligns management with the 2030 target and rewards volume acquisition.

The external forces net to a mild headwind the niches have outgrown. Demand C: US weighted clinic traffic -1.9% year on year in Q2 2026, the 17th consecutive quarter of decline (Morgan Stanley survey); Vetsource clinic volume -2.6%; pet services spending USD 79 billion in 2025; 81% of veterinarians report tougher conditions; care shifting to acute rather than routine; elective orthopaedics the most exposed category, with management guiding low-single-digit US orthopaedic organic growth for H2 2026; dental under-penetrated (80% of adult pets with periodontal disease). The company's own cycle B: turning up from a low base; Q2's 12% carries a US Specialised Nutrition campaign (Specialty Pharma about 9% underlying rather than 14%); the industry "stabilizing near a trough". Disruption D: online pharmacy (Chewy's Modern Animal), non-surgical orthopaedics (Librela, Solensia, Spryng) and AI point-of-care diagnostics (Vetscan Imagyst, IDEXX inVue Dx), each aimed at a Vimian channel or product; the injectables-versus-surgery substitution against Movora bites first; the mitigant is clinics leaning on in-clinic diagnostics and consumables (iM3, Indical). Supply side C: raw material and merchandise costs EUR 73.2m in H1 2026 against EUR 64.8m (+13%); potential US tariffs on about half of US sales for a low-single-digit percentage-point risk to EBITA; about 20% of cost of goods linked to Taiwan; a 10% combined cost rise worth about EUR 10m of operating profit. Macro C: rates and veterinary cost inflation act on the US elective business; USD 38.19% of 2025 revenue unhedged, a 10% USD move worth EUR 15.7m of revenue and EUR 2.3m of EBIT; translation -5% in Q1 2026, -1% in Q2. Competition C: tightening in broad therapeutics (Zoetis US companion-animal sales -11% in Q2 2026 with a pricing reset; dermatology share down five points to 86%) but not in the niches; the DePuy Synthes separation (USD 9.2 billion of sales, 18 to 24 months) a possible opening for Movora. Political and regulatory B: antimicrobial stewardship supportive; the UK CMA probe does not reach a clinic supplier; MSCI AAA in May 2026. Catch-all: the Delaware VOI award (USD 40.2m damages plus USD 8.6m interest; USD 31.9m paid in Q4 2025; judgment by September 2026) is a cash cushion, not a driver.

The outputs have turned at the top line and in the segment margins, not where the return is made. Revenue growth B: reported growth 17.9%, 13.0%, 13.4% over FY2023 to FY2025; consensus +12.5%, +9.8%, +8.8%, +7.2%; our modal +12%, +10%, +10%, +9% (organic 7% to 8% plus 2% to 3% bolt-ons), an increase against the last three years' organic average of about 6% at every horizon. Margin C: adjusted EBITA margin 26.3% (2023), 24.8% (2025), 25.2% (Q1 2026), 24.5% (Q2 2026 against 24.3%); reported EBIT margin 13.1% (2024), 15.7% (2025), 18.4% (Q2 2026) as comparability items fall; mix is the lever (MedTech 23.7% to 25.8%; Specialty Pharma 30.1%; Veterinary Services 28.7% to 28.2%; Diagnostics 9.2% to 9.0%); consensus EBITDA margin 28.0% to 29.0% over FY2026 to FY2028; our modal +40 basis points a year to about 26% by FY2028. Cash conversion D: FY2025 EUR 105.7m (101%, 92% excluding USD 28.7m litigation receipts); Q1 2026 EUR 23.0m against EUR 29.2m (79%); Q2 2026 EUR 3.8m against EUR 29.7m (13%) on receivables (EUR 15.7m) and tax paid (EUR 13.5m); management says receivables normalise in Q3 2026; the research's test is Q3 conversion above 60%. Net debt C: 2.1x stable; acquisitions (EUR 93.3m net in FY2025, EUR 46.4m in H1 2026) absorb the cash; a one-point rate rise costs EUR 2.0m of pre-tax profit. Sell-side upgrades C: plausible not probable; the sell-side moved from cutting (FY2026 mean earnings per share -11.5% over twelve months) to nudging up (+9.6% one month, +1.4% three months at 2026-09-18); DNB Carnegie expects consensus to follow it up by only 1% to 2%; the company gives no numerical guidance; upgrade record D (EUR 200m by 2025 abandoned; 35% margin and 30% growth goals lapsed; "an over-promiser archetype historically"; two beats of 4% under the new chief executive); revision skew C (FY2027 +3.9% over three months, +4.8% over six, -10.6% over twelve); the 2030 target is roughly double the consensus trajectory and consensus does not believe it (DNB Carnegie: 27% a year "substantially above the historical growth rate of 10%"); our FY2026 modal equals the FactSet median (EUR 0.100), FY2027 3% below (0.122 against 0.126), FY2028 7% below (0.140 against 0.150). Goldilocks growth B: about 16% a year FY2026 to FY2029 on our path (EUR 0.100 to 0.157) against consensus 17% (to 0.161); FY2027 +22% (consensus +26%) is over-extrapolation territory resting partly on tax and interest; the three-year path decelerates 22%, 15%, 12%; without the below-EBITA relief the FY2027 step is about 12% and the compound rate 11.4%, which would make this attribute C. Staircase B: near steps (the Delaware judgment by September 2026; heads in post 1 and 5 October 2026; Q3 2026 interim on 22 October 2026 with the cash test; PAX2 launch H2 2026; Japan and Portugal launches Q3 2026; two to three acquisitions by year-end); mid steps (FY2026 results February 2027; Clarity XR and dental subscription revenue; the LTIP hurdle year; the next related-party disclosure); far steps C (the 2030 halfway point; Nextmune Bio biologics with no revenue attached).
counter_case: The strongest case against is the opposite of the sell-side's: not that the recovery will fail, but that it has succeeded and does not matter. The Q2 2026 quarter was the best the new team will print for a while: a 14% Specialty Pharma number that is 9% underlying, a MedTech +11% against a -4% comparison, a Diagnostics segment at a 9% margin, and a cash-flow statement that shows what a roll-up looks like when growth is bought with receivables and earn-outs. The group's adjusted EBITA margin has not moved in three years (26.3% to 24.5%) and will not, because the model buys margin (dental at a premium) rather than earning it, and operating leverage is absent by design (thirteen people at the centre; synergies by incentive not integration; a former controller says the structure "limits large-scale cost takeouts"). The 9.4% return on invested capital is the true return of the enterprise, and the 7.5x entry multiple is a mirage once integration cost, comparability items, stay-on bonuses (EUR 2.9m to 3.9m adjusted out) and capitalised development (EUR 6.0m, about 250 basis points of adjusted EBITA margin on Jefferies' figures) are counted. The EUR 300m target exists to justify the next equity raise, of which there have been two at falling prices; the sponsor at 58% will sell into strength; the multiple, at the median now, has one direction to go when the sector's own leader is cutting guidance. The evidence is on the page: the adjusted-to-reported gap of EUR 38m in 2025 (adjusted EBITA EUR 105.3m against reported EBIT EUR 66.8m; EUR 74m between adjusted EBITA and reported net income of EUR 31.3m), the 13% cash quarter, litigation cash at 27% of 2025 operating cash flow, an employee net promoter score that is either -36% or 30 and in neither case the targeted 50, related-party licensing to an entity owned by the Specialty Pharma manager (EUR 9.4m in 2024, EUR 9.7m in 2025) disclosed and never explained, and the Barclays Sell at 2.62 EUR. The Building Block 1 form of the same argument: the acceleration is a campaign and a soft comparison, the EUR 300m target needs 23% to 27% a year against about 10% delivered, and the below-EBITA normalisation that makes FY2027 +26% on consensus is tax and interest, not business. The Building Block 2 form: the niche moats are real but do not pay, so either they are narrower than the research says or the acquisition model destroys the value they create. The Building Block 3 form: this is continuity with a new face, the strategy unchanged, the target old, no guidance increase, the acquisition engine at its old pace, so the case is at best a lapsed 'OSHQC CfC Clearing' that fits nothing crisply.

What the record concedes: the margin has not moved; the cash quarter is a real problem until the Q3 print says otherwise; the entry multiple is pre-synergy and pre-integration cost; the return on capital is the shareholder's return; the multiple's downside is larger than its upside from here; a fifth of FY2027's step on our own decomposition sits below EBITA; scale has not yet produced margin (revenue +28% over three years while the margin fell); and a bounded-downside argument on the best segment does not work: Specialty Pharma's FY2025 revenue of EUR 182.4m at its 30% margin is about EUR 55m of segment EBITA, worth EUR 660m at the core peers' 12x (35% of the EUR 1,897m enterprise value) and EUR 880m at the Nordic-compounder 16x (46%), so the segment does not cover the enterprise value at either multiple. Also conceded at Building Block 3: the strategy is sharpened rather than changed, the target is old and unmodelled, there is no guidance increase.
triggers: The Q3 2026 interim on 22 October 2026: cash conversion above 60% and North American orthopaedics at mid-single-digit growth move the re-rating branch's odds from 20% toward 35% and the 'Investment Case' from D to C; cash conversion below 60% with net working capital still above 24% of revenue at year-end 2026 invalidates the self-funding leg; two consecutive quarters below 60% invalidate. The price at or below about SEK 29 to 30 with the thesis intact re-enters the case (the eighteen-month test clears at SEK 29.4; the three-year test at SEK 26.0; the February-to-April 2026 range SEK 27.90 to 30.40 is where the case was a buy). Specialty Pharma underlying organic growth below 8% for a quarter is an alarm and below 6% for two quarters invalidates. A quarter of North American orthopaedic decline is an alarm; two invalidate; MedTech margin below 24% is an alarm. Net debt at 2.5x is an alarm, 3.0x invalidates; no acquisitions announced in H2 2026 is an alarm against the test of two to three by year-end. The multiple below 18.4x (five-year 25th percentile) is an alarm on the share-price risk; any placing below the market by the sponsor is an alarm. A tax rate above 33% or financial items above EUR 23m for FY2026 is an alarm on the below-EBITA normalisation; the three-month revision turning negative is an alarm and 2%-plus cuts with underperformance invalidate on the framework's pattern; FY2027 earnings per share below EUR 0.115 is an alarm. US clinic traffic below -3% is an alarm; a 10% adverse USD move is an alarm and a 20% USD fall (leverage past 3.0x on the stress case) invalidates. Open questions the record could not close from the folder: the live thematics file and the ticker's sidecar (not read; thematic tailwind rated on the research alone); the track-record and lessons files and the Wisdom Library (not read; seven plausible fits offered, the seventh, buying after a 36.6% six-month rise on two beats, the one expected to match a lesson); the related-party licensing, disclosed and unexplained, not load-bearing; the disputed employee net promoter score, on which nothing rests; the market's read of CVS Group's relative strength, not in the dashboard data; the sizing of the consensus dental line the earnings review's non-consensus call would beat; the second-tier earnings bases (six brokers' FY2026 adjusted estimates 0.091 to 0.140 EUR), which can move the pinned series on a single broker's change; the FY2029 consensus (+7%, one broker), a coverage artefact; the Delaware VOI judgment expected by September 2026; the Specialty Pharma and M&A heads taking post on 1 and 5 October 2026; the PAX2 launch and the Japan and Portugal launches in H2 and Q3 2026; the FY2026 results in February 2027 as the first full year under the new team and the first evidence on FY2026 cash conversion.
